meta.title: Key Equations - Deep Learning (Goodfellow et al.)

equations.name: Matrix Product
equations.description: Each entry of the product matrix is the dot product of a row of A with a column of B.

equations.name: Transpose of a Product
equations.description: The transpose of a matrix product reverses the order of the factors.

equations.name: Matrix Inverse
equations.description: A matrix multiplied by its inverse yields the identity matrix.

equations.name: Solving Linear Systems
equations.description: A system of linear equations can be solved by left-multiplying both sides by the inverse of A.

equations.name: L2 Norm (Euclidean)
equations.description: The Euclidean norm measures the ordinary straight-line distance from the origin.

equations.name: Lp Norm
equations.description: The general Lp norm family, which includes L1 (Manhattan) and L2 (Euclidean) as special cases.

equations.name: Eigendecomposition
equations.description: A square matrix can be decomposed into its eigenvalues and eigenvectors, revealing how it stretches space.

equations.name: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)
equations.description: Any matrix (including non-square) can be factored into orthogonal matrices U, V and a diagonal matrix D of singular values.

equations.name: Moore-Penrose Pseudoinverse
equations.description: Generalizes the matrix inverse to non-square or singular matrices, enabling least-squares solutions.

equations.name: Trace Cyclic Property
equations.description: The trace is invariant under cyclic permutations of the matrix product.

equations.name: Determinant from Eigenvalues
equations.description: The determinant equals the product of all eigenvalues, measuring the volume scaling factor of the linear transformation.

equations.name: Marginalization (Sum Rule)
equations.description: A marginal probability is obtained by summing (or integrating) a joint distribution over the other variables.

equations.name: Product Rule (Chain Rule of Probability)
equations.description: The joint probability of two events equals the conditional probability times the marginal.

equations.name: Bayes' Rule
equations.description: Relates the posterior probability to the likelihood and prior, forming the foundation of Bayesian inference.

equations.name: Expectation (Discrete)
equations.description: The expected value is the probability-weighted average of a function over all possible outcomes.

equations.name: Variance
equations.description: Variance measures how much a random variable's values spread around its mean.

equations.name: Gaussian (Normal) Distribution
equations.description: The most commonly used continuous distribution, parameterized by mean and variance.

equations.name: Multivariate Gaussian Distribution
equations.description: Generalizes the Gaussian to vectors, with a covariance matrix capturing correlations between dimensions.

equations.name: Shannon Entropy
equations.description: Quantifies the average amount of information (or surprise) in a probability distribution.

equations.name: KL Divergence
equations.description: Measures how much distribution P differs from a reference distribution Q; it is non-negative and asymmetric.

equations.name: Cross-Entropy
equations.description: Measures the average number of bits needed to encode data from P using a code optimized for Q.

equations.name: Softmax Function
equations.description: Converts a vector of real numbers into a valid probability distribution over discrete classes.

equations.name: Sigmoid Function
equations.description: Squashes any real value into the range (0, 1), commonly used for binary probabilities and gating.

equations.name: Gradient Descent Update
equations.description: Iteratively moves parameters in the direction of steepest descent, scaled by learning rate epsilon.

equations.name: Jacobian Matrix
equations.description: Collects all first-order partial derivatives of a vector-valued function into a matrix.

equations.name: Hessian Matrix
equations.description: The matrix of second-order partial derivatives, describing the local curvature of a scalar function.

equations.name: Second-Order Taylor Expansion
equations.description: Approximates a function locally using its value, gradient g, and Hessian H at a reference point.

equations.name: Lagrangian (Constrained Optimization)
equations.description: Converts a constrained optimization problem into an unconstrained one using Lagrange multipliers.

equations.name: Mean Squared Error (MSE)
equations.description: The average squared difference between predictions and true values, the most common regression loss.

equations.name: Estimator Bias
equations.description: The difference between an estimator's expected value and the true parameter value.

equations.name: Bias-Variance Decomposition
equations.description: Total estimation error decomposes into squared bias plus variance, capturing the underfitting-overfitting tradeoff.

equations.name: Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE)
equations.description: Finds the parameters that maximize the log-likelihood of the observed data under the model.

equations.name: MAP Estimation
equations.description: Extends MLE by incorporating a prior over parameters, equivalent to adding a regularization term.

equations.name: Linear Regression Normal Equation
equations.description: The closed-form least-squares solution for linear regression weights.

equations.name: Logistic Regression
equations.description: Models binary classification probability by passing a linear function through the sigmoid.

equations.name: Feedforward Network
equations.description: A deep network is a composition of learned functions, each layer transforming the representation from the previous one.

equations.name: Affine Transform + Activation
equations.description: Each hidden layer applies a linear transformation followed by a nonlinear activation function.

equations.name: ReLU
equations.description: The rectified linear unit, the default activation for modern deep networks due to its simplicity and non-saturating gradient.

equations.name: Leaky ReLU
equations.description: A ReLU variant that allows a small gradient when the unit is inactive, preventing dead neurons.

equations.name: Cross-Entropy Loss (Binary)
equations.description: The standard loss function for binary classification, derived from maximum likelihood of a Bernoulli model.

equations.name: Softmax Output
equations.description: Converts the output layer's logits into a normalized probability distribution over classes.

equations.name: Chain Rule (Backpropagation)
equations.equation: $$\frac{\partial L}{\partial w_{ij}^{(l)}} = \frac{\partial L}{\partial a_j^{(l)}} \cdot \frac{\partial a_j^{(l)}}{\partial w_{ij}^{(l)}}$$
equations.description: Backpropagation computes gradients layer by layer using the chain rule, enabling efficient training of deep networks.

equations.name: Gradient of Loss w.r.t. Output
equations.description: For softmax with cross-entropy, the gradient at the output layer simplifies to the difference between predictions and targets.

equations.name: L2 Regularization (Weight Decay)
equations.description: Adds a penalty proportional to the squared magnitude of weights, encouraging smaller and more diffuse weight vectors.

equations.name: L1 Regularization
equations.description: Penalizes the sum of absolute weight values, encouraging sparsity by driving some weights exactly to zero.

equations.name: Dropout (Forward Pass)
equations.description: Randomly zeroes out hidden units during training, preventing co-adaptation and acting as an ensemble approximation.

equations.name: Dropout Weight Scaling (Inference)
equations.description: At test time, weights are scaled by the keep probability to compensate for the missing dropout masks.

equations.name: Batch Normalization
equations.description: Normalizes each mini-batch to zero mean and unit variance, reducing internal covariate shift and stabilizing training.

equations.name: Batch Norm (Learnable Parameters)
equations.description: After normalization, learnable scale and shift parameters restore the network's representational power.

equations.name: SGD Update
equations.description: The simplest optimization update: move parameters in the negative gradient direction scaled by the learning rate.

equations.name: SGD with Momentum
equations.description: Accumulates a velocity vector to accelerate through flat regions and dampen oscillations in steep directions.

equations.name: Nesterov Momentum
equations.description: Evaluates the gradient at a lookahead position, providing better convergence than standard momentum.

equations.name: AdaGrad
equations.description: Adapts the learning rate per-parameter by dividing by the accumulated sum of squared gradients.

equations.name: RMSProp
equations.description: Uses an exponential moving average of squared gradients to adapt learning rates, fixing AdaGrad's diminishing rates.

equations.name: Adam Update
equations.description: Combines momentum and adaptive learning rates with bias correction, the default optimizer for most deep learning.

equations.name: Learning Rate Decay
equations.description: Gradually reduces the learning rate over training to allow fine-grained convergence near a minimum.

equations.name: Xavier Initialization
equations.description: Initializes weights to maintain variance across layers, preventing signal from exploding or vanishing at initialization.

equations.name: 1D Convolution
equations.description: Applies a filter by sliding it across a 1D input and computing weighted sums at each position.

equations.name: 2D Convolution
equations.description: The fundamental operation of CNNs: slides a 2D kernel across an image, computing local weighted sums.

equations.name: Cross-Correlation
equations.description: What deep learning frameworks actually compute — convolution without flipping the kernel.

equations.name: Convolution Output Size
equations.description: Computes the spatial dimension of a convolution output given input size n, kernel size k, padding p, and stride s.

equations.name: Conv Layer Parameter Count
equations.description: The number of learnable parameters in a convolutional layer, including bias terms.

equations.name: RNN Hidden State
equations.description: The core recurrence relation: each hidden state is a function of the previous state and the current input.

equations.name: Vanilla RNN
equations.description: The standard RNN update equation with tanh activation, simple but prone to vanishing gradients.

equations.name: RNN Output
equations.description: Produces a probability distribution at each time step by applying softmax to a linear transform of the hidden state.

equations.name: BPTT Gradient
equations.description: Backpropagation through time sums the gradient contributions from every time step in the sequence.

equations.name: LSTM Forget Gate
equations.description: Controls how much of the previous cell state to retain, enabling LSTMs to learn long-range dependencies.

equations.name: LSTM Cell State Update
equations.description: The cell state is updated by forgetting some old information and adding new candidate values gated by the input gate.

equations.name: GRU Update
equations.description: A simplified gated architecture that interpolates between the previous state and a candidate using a single update gate.

equations.name: Gradient Vanishing Condition
equations.description: When the Jacobian of the hidden state transition has norm less than 1, gradients shrink exponentially over time steps.
